beginner.summary: For web and full-stack developers who know JavaScript or TypeScript and have never shipped a Firebase backend. Covers the Firebase project model, the Firebase CLI and Local Emulator Suite, the modular Web SDK, Cloud Firestore documents, queries and real-time listeners, Firebase Authentication, Firestore and Cloud Storage Security Rules with unit tests, Hosting preview channels, Realtime Database basics, first Cloud Functions, the Spark and Blaze plans, and a real-time task board capstone.
prerequisites: Writes JavaScript or TypeScript with ES modules, async/await and npm, and can read JSON
Uses git and a terminal, and has Node.js (current LTS) and a code editor installed
Has a Google account and can create a Firebase project in the console (a payment card is only needed in the Blaze-plan day)
outcomes: Create, configure and deploy a Firebase project from the Firebase CLI and develop against the Local Emulator Suite without touching production data
Read, write, query and listen to Cloud Firestore data and authenticate users with email and Google sign-in from the modular Web SDK
Write and unit-test Security Rules for Firestore and Cloud Storage so that the default posture is deny
Ship a real-time web application with Hosting, a first Cloud Function and cost guardrails

intermediate.summary: For developers who have built a first Firebase app and now need production-grade data models, access control and server logic. Covers Firestore modelling and indexing, transactions and counters, aggregation queries, role-based rules with custom claims, Admin SDK tokens and sessions, multi-factor authentication, callable, background, scheduled and task-queue functions, secrets and function configuration, App Check, Remote Config and A/B testing, FCM HTTP v1, backups and TTL, Hosting rewrites, App Hosting, emulator-based CI and a multi-tenant SaaS capstone.
